title: test-0022-SCI-PHY-MOTION9
passage: In physics, we must distinguish between speed and velocity. Speed is simply the rate of change of distance, representing how fast an object moves. Velocity, however, is speed in a specific direction. If a car drives around a circular track at a constant speed of 40 km/h, its velocity is constantly changing because its direction changes at every point. This change in velocity means the car is accelerating, even though its speed remains steady. Acceleration is defined as the rate of change of velocity over time. It is not limited to speeding up; it also includes slowing down or changing direction. Furthermore, we must be careful with graphs. On a velocity-time graph, a horizontal line indicates that the velocity is constant, not that the object is at rest. If an object moves from point A to point B and returns to point A, its total displacement is zero, even though it has traveled a significant distance. Displacement measures the shortest path between the initial and final positions, whereas distance is the total path length covered. Understanding these differences is crucial for analyzing motion correctly, as distance and displacement are rarely the same value in real-world scenarios.
summary: If a car goes around a circular track at 40 km/h, its direction changes every time it goes around, so its velocity is always changing. This means the car is accelerating, even though its speed stays the same.
